mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where real GDP growth declines over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production is associated with higher economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where industrial production increases by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 2% in a month indicates a weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is a major driver of economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where retail and food services sales decrease by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payroll employment by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as increased employment is associated with higher consumer spending and economic activity.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where nonfarm payroll employment increases by more than 200,000 within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and retail sales by more than 1% each within a month signals a strengthening demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as both indicators are associated with increased economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both housing starts and retail sales increase by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in a month signals a potential deflationary pressure, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as deflationary environments are typically associated with economic contractions.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the consumer price index decreases by more than 0.5% within a month.
